executiveSummary: Active campaigns are targeting Siemens S7 PLCs using AI-generated scripts over S7comm (TCP/102), creating immediate risk of process manipulation in Water/Wastewater, Energy, and Manufacturing environments Security Advisory . U.S. agencies report Iranian-affiliated actors exploiting internet-exposed PLCs (Rockwell, Schneider, Siemens), modifying logic, disabling alarms, and falsifying HMI data-confirmed operational disruptions are noted Security Advisory . Credential data for tens of thousands of Fortinet FortiGate devices ("FortiBleed") is circulating among threat actors; cracked admin hashes and reused VPN creds enable rapid perimeter compromise and AD pivoting Security Advisory . Researchers demonstrated AI-assisted porting of a pre-auth RCE to additional WAGO PLC models (Nucleus FTP server), achieving ARM shellcode and even bricking a controller-underscoring low-cost exploit transfer across PLC lines View Article . State actors continue to abuse edge infrastructure: FSB Center 16 campaigns exploit misconfigured routers; China-nexus operations leverage covert botnets of SOHO/IoT devices to mask activity and pre-position in CI CISA Advisory CISA Advisory . Critical perimeter vulnerabilities demand immediate action: NetScaler ADC/Gateway pre-auth RCE (CVE-2026-8452) and SonicWall SMA 1000 (actively exploited SSRF+RCE) threaten remote-access paths into OT Security Advisory CERT-FR Alert . Supply-chain exposure escalates: actively exploited auth-bypass in JFrog Artifactory enables admin token minting and artifact tampering-risking poisoned OT firmware/builds down the chain View Article . Multiple high-impact OT/ICS CVE clusters in weekly bulletins: OPC UA (Eclipse Milo) auth bypass/diagnostics exposure/DoS, EVSE (OCPP) RCEs, PLC stacks (Modbus, EtherNet/IP) manipulation/DoS, and industrial drives unsigned-code risks CISA Weekly CISA Weekly .

relevance: Threat activity this cycle directly targets core industrial control assets (PLCs) and the perimeter infrastructure that frequently brokers access to OT networks. Concurrent campaigns (Iran-, Russia-, and China-linked) and exploited supply-chain platforms (artifacts/repos) increase the probability of process disruption and unauthorized command execution. Multiple ICS protocol/stack weaknesses (S7comm, EtherNet/IP/CIP, OPC UA, Modbus/TCP) elevate the value of zone-based segmentation and protocol-aware allowlisting. Transportation and energy-adjacent risks extend to EV charging infrastructure and railway signaling, underscoring the need for strict OT network isolation and rigorous change control on controllers and HMIs.

items: OPC UA (Eclipse Milo): authorization bypass, diagnostics exposure, and multiple DoS vectors-patch libraries and embedded products immediately CISA Weekly .
EVSE/Charging: Autel MaxiCharger OCPP/WebSocket RCE; EVbee OCPP/USB/NFC issues-segment charge points and enforce mTLS CISA Weekly .
Industrial drives/PLCs and protocol stacks: Danfoss iC7 unsigned code risk; EtherNet/IP OpENer buffer overflow; Modbus/PLC DoS/manipulation CISA Weekly .
Perimeter access: NetScaler ADC/Gateway (CVE-2026-8452) pre-auth RCE-fixed versions required; remove public exposure JPCERT/CC .
Supply-chain: JFrog Artifactory Access auth-bypass actively exploited-upgrade to 7.161.20; audit tokens/users View Article .

descriptions: Initial Access: exploitation of edge devices (VPN/ADC/SMA) (T1190), use of compromised SOHO routers as covert relays (TA0001).
Discovery/Pivot: SNMP misconfig harvest and config copy via TFTP/FTP (T1046/T1005), scanning for exposed PLC/HMIs (T1595.002).
Execution: AI-generated scripts using snap7 over S7comm (TCP/102) to read/write memory (T1059), EtherNet/IP/CIP malformed packets for faults/DoS.
Persistence: Web shells on gateways/servers (T1505), app passwords and IMAP in Zimbra (T1098), router config backdoors (T1547).
Defense Evasion: Use of residential/SOHO proxies; traffic mirroring on routers; encrypted C2 via DNS/HTTPS with rapid cert churn.
Impact: controller mode changes, alarm suppression, logic tampering, and EVSE remote manipulation (ICS: Impair Process Control).

outlook72h: Expect continued scanning and exploitation for Siemens S7 PLCs and exposed HMIs; watch for opportunistic weaponization of NetScaler ADC pre-auth RCE. FortiGate credential reuse will likely drive VPN spray and device-admin attempts-monitor for anomalous logins and config exports. Supply-chain targeting (Artifactory) may expand, prompting artifact poisoning risks; validate CI/CD integrity and restrict build servers' egress. EVSE/OCPP probing is expected to increase-tighten charger segmentation and enforce OCPP security profiles.
